description: Browser incremental game UI + growing set of real mechanics (Workers, Gold, Wood, Stone, Builder's Bench, Market), built on a reusable core engine supporting simple resource cards, multi-track 'build other things' cards, and a repeatable sell-for-gold card.

golden_rules.note: Standing rules Claude follows every session. Confirmed by user. Apply regardless of what else is being worked on.
rules: Never assume on ambiguity. Always ask clarifying questions, numbered, before writing any code.
Warn the user when context window usage reaches 75%, stated in all caps: 'MY CONTEXT WINDOW IS 75% FULL.'
Always deliver a full zip of every project file in the correct folder structure, every time work is delivered — not just the files that changed. This includes the summary and this manifest.
Keep code as clean and line-reduced as possible while still fully achieving the goal.

Mechanic/script loading uses manual <script> tags in index.html (grouped, commented) — never a dynamic loader. index.html must always be the ground-truth, one-file list of what's active and in what order.
Per-mechanic files (js/mechanics/*.js) contain ONLY that mechanic's data/numbers plus minimal glue code. All shared behavior lives once in js/core/ and is never duplicated per mechanic.
The context footer (js/core/footer.js) is the one area Claude has standing permission to add to proactively, without asking first, as new mechanics are built.
Wood (js/mechanics/wood.js) is the reference template for the 'Resource Card' pattern. Any future resource card should reuse Wood's exact architecture, substituting only that mechanic's own data.

numbers_policy.note: This manifest deliberately does NOT duplicate tunable numbers (rates, costs, build times, caps, starting amounts, sell bundle sizes/gold rates) — those live only in their owning file and are edited there directly, including by the user without Claude's help. This manifest documents SHAPE and RULES (how systems behave), not values. Applies equally to Market's ladder/sell-resource data as it does to Wood/Stone/Bench. Where a number is needed for context, the manifest names the file to check instead of the number itself.

files.index.html: Markup skeleton — layout, cheat header, context footer, settings gear, settings modal, one reusable card-detail modal. Modal header is now two rows: .modal-header-top (steppers slot | title | close button) plus #card-modal-header-sub below it (generic subtitle slot, see card_detail_modal.header_slots). Manual script tags grouped by role, market.js included after buildersbench.js.
files.style.css: All visual tokens and component styles. Mobile breakpoint at 700px. Owns the fixed-square card sizing pattern used by Market's sell cards (see sell_track) — check this file directly for current pixel values, not this manifest.
files.script.js: Core shell behavior only: modal open/close, section collapse, settings menu, placeholder-toggle wiring. openCardModal(name, descriptionHtml, headerLeftEl, subtitleHtml) gained a 4th optional argument written into #card-modal-header-sub.
files.placeholders.js: All demo/example content, fully isolated. Unchanged.
files.js/core/resources.js: Generic left-hand resource registry. hidden:true at registration + Resources.reveal(id). add() routes through Upgrades.collectIntoReservations() first. Unchanged this round.
files.js/core/workers.js: Generic worker pool — unchanged. Starting total/idle counts live here.
files.js/core/upkeep.js: Gold drain per tick. New: mechanics can set upkeepExempt=true (used by Market) to skip gold drain entirely for their assigned workers, regardless of resource-cap state.
files.js/core/upgrades.js: Now exposes THREE track factories (see multi_track_engine): create() for sequential ladders, createChoiceTrack() for independent-choice single-slot lists, and createSellTrack() (new) for repeatable sell-for-gold cards. The delegated action listener now binds to 'click' (not 'pointerdown' — see modal_architecture.click_convention) and resolves composite track keys. create()'s renderModalHTML() gained an optional arrowHTML 4th argument to inject a collapse arrow inline into the active tier's name row (see collapsible_ladder_layout).
files.js/core/cards.js: Generic real-card builder. Optional second progress bar (getBuildBarPct), onOpen() hook, startHidden + Cards.reveal(), getWorkerDesc() hook. New: mechanic.modalWide opt-in flag widens the shared modal. New: refresh() now patches the open modal's live text via patchOpenModal() instead of replacing its innerHTML every tick — see modal_architecture.patch_vs_rebuild. rebuildOpenModal() (full innerHTML replace) is only called from refreshOpenModal(), itself only called after a user action fires. patchOpenModal() now also calls an optional generic mechanic.patchLiveTrack() hook every tick (renamed/generalized this round from a Market-only patchSellCards) — any mechanic's second/third track uses this same hook name to live-patch its own rows.
files.js/core/cheats.js: Cheat menu — Wood/Stone/Gold +100, Workers +5, speed toggles. Unchanged this round.
files.js/mechanics/wood.js: Wood data + status glue. THE reference template for the Resource Card pattern. Exposes getWorkerDesc(), patchUpgradeCost(), patchBuildStatus() (both delegate to the track's getResourceTracker()/getBuildStatusText()). Current rate table/costs: see this file directly.
files.js/mechanics/stone.js: Second Resource Card, built from Wood's exact template. Starts hidden — revealed only when Builder's Bench completes Stone Pit. Same patch hooks as Wood. Current rate table/costs: see this file directly.
files.js/mechanics/buildersbench.js: Not a resource — no left-hand row. Starts hidden, permanently revealed once wood reaches a threshold. Owns a self-upgrade ladder + Construction list. Construction's Market item renamed 'Market Stall'; completing it reveals the Market mechanic's card (Market's own starting tier is instant/pre-built, like Bench's own). Current tier tables/costs: see this file directly.
files.js/mechanics/market.js: NEW. Not a resource — no left-hand row. upkeepExempt=true, modalWide=true. Owns a self-upgrade ladder (same collapsible pattern as Bench) plus a sell track (Upgrades.createSellTrack) for Wood/Stone/Simple Parts/Simple Tools/Plywood/Brick. getSubtitleHtml() supplies the modal header's two subtitle lines (an upgrade tip, removed once Wood or Stone gets its first upgrade, and a note that Market's workers are always upkeep-free). Starts hidden, revealed + instant-built when Builder's Bench completes 'Market Stall'. Current tier ladder, sell-resource list, bundle sizes, and gold rates: see this file directly.
files.js/main.js: Wires real resources/cards into DOM and starts loop. Camp grid build order: Wood, Stone, Builder's Bench, Market (Stone/Bench/Market all start hidden via CSS display:none until revealed).

structure: #cheat-header (hidden by default, flex row, pushed by settings toggle)
#left-hand-real-resources — Workers, Gold, Wood, Stone rows (Stone hidden until revealed)
.section-label 'Camp' + #grid-camp (.card-grid): Wood, Stone (hidden until revealed), Builder's Bench (hidden until revealed), Market (hidden until revealed)

header_slots.subtitle_row: #card-modal-header-sub — NEW, generic slot below the top row. Filled by an optional mechanic.getSubtitleHtml() hook, passed through openCardModal's new 4th argument. Auto-hides via :empty when a mechanic doesn't define the hook. Currently only Market uses this.

card_detail_modal.api: window.OrbWeaver.openCardModal(name, descriptionHtml, headerLeftEl, subtitleHtml) — headerLeftEl optional DOM node, subtitleHtml optional string (NEW 4th arg). window.OrbWeaver.Cards.closeModal() force-closes it.

modal_close_rules.note: Whether clicking an upgrade-modal button closes the modal depends on the action and track type, decided in upgrades.js's delegated click listener (see modal_architecture.click_convention for why it's click, not pointerdown).
closes_modal: 'start' on a sequential track (Wood/Stone/self-upgrade 'Build upgrade') — but ONLY if the player could fully afford it, so the track jumped straight to the building phase. If they couldn't fully afford it (now collecting), the modal stays open.
'start' on a choice track (Construction's 'Build' button) — always closes, regardless of afford state.
stays_open: every Market sell-card action ('select-bundle', 'sell', 'cancel-sale', 'toggle-auto', 'toggle-lock') — selling is repeatable, not a one-shot commitment

modal_architecture.patch_vs_rebuild: An open modal must never have its full body innerHTML replaced on a per-tick basis — only specific text nodes get patched. Rebuilding the whole HTML 5x/second was destroying and recreating every button in the modal; a tap landing between rebuilds had nowhere to register, silently failing. Standing fix: Cards.refresh() (called every tick) calls patchOpenModal(), which only updates elements a mechanic exposes via optional hooks — patchUpgradeCost(), patchBuildStatus(), patchSellCards() — creating/destroying no DOM nodes. rebuildOpenModal() (full innerHTML replace, via renderModalHTML()) is only invoked from refreshOpenModal(), itself only called after a user action fires a button press, when the structure genuinely changes. Any new mechanic needing live-updating modal content should add a small patch*() hook rather than relying on renderModalHTML() being re-run every tick.
modal_architecture.click_convention: Every element with [data-upgrade-action] is wired through a single delegated 'click' listener in upgrades.js, never 'pointerdown'. pointerdown previously let a modal-closing action's stray follow-up click land on whatever card was newly exposed underneath, opening an unrelated card's modal right after the tap. 'click' requires pointerdown+pointerup on the same element, matching how card-opening already works, preventing this.

collapsible_ladder_layout.note: Shared layout pattern for both Builder's Bench and Market's self-upgrade ladder (Upgrades.create(table, renderEffect, collapsible=true)). Reusable for any future collapsible mechanic.
collapsible_ladder_layout.arrow: No standalone 'Upgrades' section header. The collapse arrow is passed as create()'s renderModalHTML 4th arg (arrowHTML) and rendered inline at the left edge of the active tier's own name, nudged into the modal's side margin, so the upgrade card sits at the very top of its section.
collapsible_ladder_layout.expanded: Name/cost on one line, effect description below, action button below that — unchanged from the original layout.
collapsible_ladder_layout.collapsed: The action button ('Build upgrade' / 'Collect Resources') moves inline into the title row, flex-stretching to fill whatever width the tier name doesn't use. The live resource-cost tracker and effect description share one line below, each shrinking (text-overflow:ellipsis) rather than wrapping.
collapsible_ladder_layout.section_dividers: Builder's Bench's Construction header is now a silent divider (rule only, no 'Construction' text label) since the section is self-evident from its content. Market keeps a text label ('Sell') above its sell-card grid since that isn't otherwise obvious.

card_face_states.note: Generic pattern any Resource Card should follow (Wood/Stone both implement this) — not a Builder's Bench-only concept.
resource_card_stat_text: Stopped (no gold or at cap), not collecting → 'Stopped'
buildersbench_stat_text: Self-upgrade timer running, not collecting → empty string (top bar shows progress silently)
market_stat_text: A sale running + self-upgrade collecting → 'Selling – {n}s – Collecting'

reveal_hide_system.note: Generic mechanism for any card/resource that should start invisible until a condition is met. Reusable for any future gated content.
reveal_hide_system.resource_row: Resources.register(id, {...}, hidden: true) starts the row invisible; Resources.reveal(id) shows it permanently.
reveal_hide_system.card: mechanic.startHidden = true starts the card invisible (DOM node still built at load, display:none); Cards.reveal(mechanic) shows it permanently.
reveal_hide_system.trigger_pattern: The revealing mechanic checks its own condition inside its own tick(), guarded by a local 'already revealed' boolean so it only fires once.
reveal_hide_system.current_uses: Stone (hidden until Builder's Bench completes Stone Pit); Builder's Bench itself (hidden until wood reaches a threshold); Market (hidden until Builder's Bench completes its Construction item, renamed 'Market Stall' — Market's own starting tier is instant/pre-built on reveal, mirroring Bench's own starting tier).

multi_track_engine.note: js/core/upgrades.js supports THREE track factories. A mechanic can mix any of these under composite keys ('mechanicId:trackName'), letting one card run more than one independent process off a single worker pool — every assigned worker contributes to ALL of that card's tracks simultaneously, no splitting.
multi_track_engine.composite_track_keys: Upgrades.registerTrack(id, track) accepts any string key. Buttons/bars stamp a matching data-track attribute so the delegated listener and modal-bar smoothing loop resolve the correct track/bar. Omitting data-track (Wood/Stone) resolves to the plain mechanic id.
multi_track_engine.sequential_track (Upgrades.create): The original Wood/Stone pattern: fixed ladder, current tier always index 0, 'next 3' shown. Optional custom renderEffect(row, prevRow, liveStats, i); optional 'collapsible' flag (see collapsible_ladder_layout); optional arrowHTML 4th arg on renderModalHTML to inject the collapse arrow inline (new this round, replacing a separate label-row arrow).
multi_track_engine.choice_track (Upgrades.createChoiceTrack: For a short list of independently-buildable items sharing one build slot (Construction: Stone Pit, Market Stall, Scout's Pen, Gambler's Mat). Full cost paid up front; only one item mid-build at a time; items may start unavailable or hidden behind a gold-cost early reveal; one-time builds, drop off the list once built. onComplete(itemId, item) callback lets the mechanic react. NEW: patchModalRows() live-patches cost trackers, disabled-button state, and the active item's countdown/bar every tick (each row's outer .upgrade-row now carries data-item for targeting) — wired via the mechanic's patchLiveTrack() hook.

sell_track (Upgrades.createSellTrack) —.resources: Each defined resource has one or two selectable bundle sizes (one selected at a time) and a derived '→ N Gold' payout. Starts locked; the owning mechanic's ladder tiers call unlockResource/enableAuto/setBundles/setMaxConcurrent as they complete — the same pattern Builder's Bench uses to unlock Construction items.
sell_track (Upgrades.createSellTrack) —.sale_lifecycle: Full bundle cost paid up front (mirrors Construction's up-front rule). Pays out gold on a timer. An in-progress sale can be canceled for a full refund; refund overflowing a resource's cap is lost (same rule as gold overflow past cap being lost).
sell_track (Upgrades.createSellTrack) —.live_worker_adjustment: Sale duration is NOT frozen at sale start — recomputed every tick from the mechanic's CURRENT assigned worker count, so adding/removing workers mid-sale speeds up or slows the remaining time live, and can finish a sale early.
sell_track (Upgrades.createSellTrack) —.concurrency: A single shared pool of 'sale slots' (starts at 1, raised by ladder tiers) caps how many sales — manual or auto, any resource — can run at once. Auto-sell toggles are capped at the same slot count: toggling more on than there are slots bumps the extra toggle back off (a CSS class-toggle animation, not JS-driven, kept lightweight). Each auto-capable resource has a lock button that keeps auto-sell on through a gold-cap loss that would otherwise disable it automatically.
sell_track (Upgrades.createSellTrack) —.reserved_layout: Every sell-card resource reserves the same fixed layout space (including the auto-toggle column) whether or not that feature is unlocked yet, so unlocking something never shifts or resizes anything already on screen. The top row's reserved height was enlarged this round to fix 2-line bundle-chip wraps clipping into the gold line below (see style.css .sell-row-top).
sell_track (Upgrades.createSellTrack) —.live_sell_time_label: The 'Sell' section header shows a live '— {n.n}s' readout of the sell track's current effective duration (config.getAssigned()-adjusted), patched every tick via patchDOM() as workers change.
sell_track (Upgrades.createSellTrack) —.live_afford_state: patchDOM() now also live-toggles each idle sell card's Bundle button (disabled/enabled) as the player's resources change, not just on the next full rebuild.

multi_track_engine.resourceTracker_format: Sequential and choice tracks render live cost/time as '{amount}/{need} {Resource} {amount}/{need} {Resource} – {n}s'. Shared format, not track-specific.

fixed_square_card_pattern.note: Reusable pattern for any card in a grid-style modal body (currently only Market's sell cards). See style.css for actual pixel values.
fixed_square_card_pattern.mechanism: Explicit pixel width AND height (not derived from content) plus aspect-ratio:1 as a redundant safety net. Every internal row has its own reserved height so no state change (more/fewer bundle options, an auto-toggle unlocking, a sale starting) can resize the box.

small_opt_in_flags.upkeepExempt: mechanic.upkeepExempt = true skips gold upkeep entirely for that card's assigned workers, regardless of resource-cap state. Used by Market.
small_opt_in_flags.modalWide: mechanic.modalWide = true widens the shared modal for grid-style bodies. Applied/cleared generically by the shell on open — no mechanic-specific code in the shell.

worker_double_duty: When a mechanic runs two tracks (e.g. Builder's Bench, Market), every worker assigned to that card contributes to BOTH tracks simultaneously at full effect each tick — no splitting workers between tracks.

progress_bar_smoothing.approach: requestAnimationFrame loop per mechanic card, started once in cards.js build(). Interpolates shown% toward target% over getIntervalMs() ms. Up to two bars per mechanic (upgradeBar always, optional buildBar if getBuildBarPct() defined), each independently eased and matched to its modal progress-bar element via data-track.
progress_bar_smoothing.css: No CSS transition on either bar — JS owns all animation.

fonts.brand_display: Cinzel Decorative — Settings modal title only

not_yet_implemented: Simple Parts, Simple Tools, Plywood, Brick, Iron, Wrought Iron as actual resources — Market's sell cards for these appear once their ladder tier unlocks them, but are unsellable (player has 0) until the resource itself is built elsewhere
Market's Bazaar / Mall / Grand Bazaar / Mega Mall tiers have no special effect defined yet beyond a faster worker rate
Scout's Pen and Gambler's Mat appear as built once constructed but have no gameplay effect yet (inert by design)
Builder's Bench's self-upgrade tiers beyond Builder's Shed have placeholder 'Unlocks: TBD' effect text pending definition
Raising gold cap through normal gameplay
handoff_instructions: To continue in a new chat: upload this manifest + UI-SHELL-SUMMARY.md + the full zip of all project files. Paste the golden rules from this manifest into the first message. This manifest deliberately omits tunable numbers (see numbers_policy) — Claude should read the actual mechanic files directly for current rates/costs/times rather than assuming anything from memory of a prior session.
